East Bristol Liveable Neighbourhood · Evidence map

The roads that carried the through traffic were left out of the scheme's headline figure

Bristol City Council's March 2022 survey traced vehicles across Barton Hill, Redfield and St George. Its 2024-25 trial only counted them, at different places and under different road labels. This map sets the council's two sets of data side by side.

Start the story ↓

11 chapters · about 4 minutes

1 · The scheme

Residential streets closed to through motor traffic

11modal filters (planters and bollards)
3bus gates; one removed in May 2026

The council installed the measures in phases from 28 October 2024 to 15 August 2025. The Marsh Lane bus gate was removed in May 2026, after the trial.

Positions: OpenStreetMap. Dates: council installation summary, monitoring data pack.

2 · Before the scheme

In 2022 the council traced every vehicle across the area

21number-plate cameras, four days in March 2022
72% · 77%through traffic on Netham Road and Blackswarth Road

A vehicle seen at one boundary camera and then another within 10 minutes counts as through traffic. Each camera is labelled with its share. Most of the measured through traffic was on the two roads in the middle of the area: Netham Road and Blackswarth Road.

Council ANPR survey, March 2022, released under an information request.

3 · The reclassification

Those two roads were then classed as boundary roads

Drag the slider. On the left, the 2022 survey treats Netham Road and Blackswarth Road as internal streets (blue). On the right, the trial monitoring draws them as boundary roads (orange), as on Map 2 of the council's Monitoring Report.

77%fall on "internal roads" reported by the council
0released documents that record why the corridor was reclassified

The corridor carried most of the 2022 through traffic. As a boundary road it is outside the "internal roads" behind the headline 77 percent. The Netham Road sensor fell about 16 percent.

4 · The headline figure

Most "internal" sensors sat at the closures themselves

13 of 16internal trial sensors sit at a filter or bus gate
−36 to −99%their change, Oct 2024 to Oct 2025

Where a street is closed, most vehicles can no longer pass the sensor, so a large fall is built in. The trial sensors count vehicles; they do not show where those journeys went. The other internal sensors: Ducie Rd +5%; Great Western Lane +245%; Morton St -56%.

Council VivaCity sensors, weekday 07:00 to 19:00, data pack.

5 · Where the traffic went

The one unfiltered street beside the bus gates

+245%Great Western Lane, 368 to 1,271 vehicles a weekday

A filter planned here was dropped in October 2023. It is the only place the Monitoring Report uses the words "through traffic": the lane "is being used by through traffic due to a gap in the scheme". The Marsh Lane bus gate was removed after this increase.

6 · The bus-gate streets

What the 2022 survey found where the gates went

14 to 19%Avonvale Road through traffic
36%Marsh Lane
nonePile Marsh: no camera

The June 2023 Outline Business Case said Avonvale Road had "around 20%" passing traffic, close to the survey's figures. Pile Marsh had no camera, so its through traffic was never measured.

7 · What councillors were told

"Around 65-70%" against the council's own survey

65 to 70%through traffic on internal roads, Transport Chair, 7 July 2026
17%measured in 2022 on the internal streets outside the corridor; 24% corrected

With a 6-minute definition the 2022 figure is 8 to 11 percent. The two figures cover different streets, dates and instruments. The council did not disclose the difference, and its own paper calls the 65 to 70 percent an assumption derived from volume changes.

Appendix A3 to the July 2026 committee papers; officer response to PQ 68, 14 July 2026.

8 · The cycle route

Wesley Way: measured at both ends

44 to 106vehicles a weekday using the whole route, after correction
1.5 to 3%of the traffic at the east-end cameras

Cameras stood at both ends of Beaufort Road and Victoria Avenue. Almost all the matched vehicles were westbound, most before 09:00. Other side streets had no cameras, so these are minimum figures.

9 · A road with no trial counter

Troopers Hill Road almost doubled

1,866vehicles a weekday, March 2022
3,678March 2026, same section: +97%

The trial had no counter on this road, and the council's Methodology Note says such streets "do not have pre-trial survey count data available". The council's own 2022 survey counted it. The count shows volume, not the reason for it.

10 · The main road

Church Road was never traced

+22%NO2 at Church Road, the largest rise in the air quality table
1fatal collision, 22 April 2025, St Philips Causeway

Church Road had no camera in 2022, so journeys along it could not be traced. The Monitoring Report lists fewer collisions among its objectives but reports no collision figures.

How the figures were produced

  • Through traffic (2022): a vehicle whose number plate was recorded at one boundary camera and then at another within 10 minutes. "Corrected" figures adjust for vehicles the cameras missed, using each camera's measured capture rate.
  • Trial sensors (2024-25): weekday motor vehicles 07:00 to 19:00 at the council's VivaCity sensors, October 2024 against October 2025. Sensors count vehicles passing; they do not identify journeys.
  • Road classes: 2022 from the survey contractor's camera classes; 2024-25 redrawn from Map 2 of the Monitoring Report (printed page 8) onto OpenStreetMap roads.
  • Measures: positions from OpenStreetMap; dates from the council's installation summary. The summary also lists Victoria Avenue Middle (not yet mapped) and Grindell Road civil works; Mildred Street is mapped but not listed.

Full methods and sources: East Bristol Liveable Neighbourhood: Evidence Behind the Through-Traffic Claim, Ali Bin Shahid, October 2026.
